title: Turbocharger Underboost
fullDescription:
Power Stroke 6.0L is famous for sticky turbo vanes from soot buildup. 6.4L uses sequential turbos with similar issues. 6.7L uses single VGT.

P0299 sets when commanded vs actual boost is below threshold for set time. Often resolved with turbo cleaning or actuator replacement.

fixSteps.title: Pressure test charge air
fixSteps.instruction: 25 psi shop air, listen for hisses.

fixSteps.title: Force regen and Italian tune-up
fixSteps.instruction: Hard pulls under load can free vanes; some success.

fixSteps.title: Replace VGT solenoid (6.0L)
fixSteps.instruction: Bolt-on, located on top of turbo.

fixSteps.title: Pull turbo and clean unison ring (6.0L)
fixSteps.instruction: Soak vanes in cleaner, free with light tapping; reassemble carefully.

whenToCallPro: 6.4L sequential turbo and 6.7L cab-off jobs are dealer territory.

faq.a: Safe at operating temp, can free mildly stuck 6.0L vanes.

title: Turbocharger Boost System Performance
shortDescription: Boost system not performing as expected over operating range.
fullDescription:
Common on 6.0L Power Stroke from sooted turbo unison ring. Engine still drives but lacks pulling power and may fail emissions tests.

Fix sequence: VGT solenoid, then turbo cleaning, then turbo replacement.

fixSteps.title: Boost data log
fixSteps.instruction: Use Ford IDS or aftermarket scanner, log desired vs actual boost in WOT pull.

fixSteps.title: Replace VGT solenoid first (6.0L)
fixSteps.instruction: Inexpensive part, often resolves the code.

fixSteps.title: Replace VGT actuator (6.7L)
fixSteps.instruction: Bolt-on smart actuator with TSB programming.

whenToCallPro: 6.7L VGT actuator requires Ford IDS programming.

faq.a: Power is reduced but truck remains drivable.

title: DEF Heater A Control Circuit Performance
shortDescription: DEF tank heater is not heating as expected.
fullDescription:
6.7L Power Stroke uses a heater in the DEF tank to thaw frozen fluid. P20BA sets when ECM detects the heater is drawing current but coolant or fluid temp is not rising.

Common failure: DEF header unit heater element burns out.

fixSteps.title: Verify coolant lines to DEF header
fixSteps.instruction: Check both lines for flow and warmth.

fixSteps.title: Replace DEF header unit
fixSteps.instruction: Drain DEF, remove header from top of tank, install new with new gasket.

fixSteps.title: Reset adaptations
fixSteps.instruction: Ford IDS clear codes and run DEF system test.

whenToCallPro: Cold-region trucks may need full tank assembly replacement.

faq.a: Code can set in summer too but symptoms only show in cold weather.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low
fullDescription:
6.4L and 6.7L use common rail high-pressure fuel system. P0087 sets when actual lags target.

6.7L uses Bosch CP4 pump with similar disaster failure profile to Duramax LML; check filter for metal first.

fixSteps.title: Replace fuel filters
fixSteps.instruction: 6.7L has frame and engine filter; replace both.

fixSteps.title: Cut and inspect filters for metal
fixSteps.instruction: Metal indicates CP4 disaster, full system replacement needed.

fixSteps.title: Run rail pressure data log
fixSteps.instruction: Ford IDS or Forscan, watch crank pressure climb.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump and contaminated parts
fixSteps.instruction: If metal found, full disaster repair kit.

whenToCallPro: CP4 disaster is dealer or specialist territory.

faq.a: Aftermarket bypass kit on return line is recommended for 2011+ 6.7L.

title: Glow Plug Cylinder 1 Circuit
shortDescription: Open or shorted glow plug circuit on cylinder 1.
fullDescription:
Power Stroke uses individual glow plug drivers in the GPCM. P0671 indicates the cylinder 1 plug is electrically failed.

Glow plug failures on 6.0L can swell tips that break off into the cylinder, requiring head removal. Replace promptly.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test glow plug
fixSteps.instruction: Spec ~0.6 ohms; open or high resistance means replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace glow plug
fixSteps.instruction: Use anti-seize, torque to spec (10 Nm typical), do not over-tighten or tip will break.

fixSteps.title: Replace harness if damaged
fixSteps.instruction: Glow plug harness sits under valve cover on 6.0L.

whenToCallPro: If a tip has broken off into the cylinder.
videoSearchQuery: Power Stroke P0671 glow plug replacement

faq.a: Above 32F engine will start, below freezing it will struggle.

title: DPF Efficiency Below Threshold
fullDescription:
6.4L and 6.7L Power Stroke monitor DPF efficiency. P2002 typically follows a cracked or melted substrate from a runaway regen, or a removed/gutted filter.

Replacement is the typical fix; inspection through ports confirms damage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect DPF visually
fixSteps.instruction: Borescope through O2 sensor port, look for cracks and missing cells.

fixSteps.title: Confirm with delta-P data
fixSteps.instruction: Near zero pressure drop at high RPM means failed filter.

fixSteps.title: Replace DPF
fixSteps.instruction: Remove with V-band clamps, install OEM unit, reset DPF service in IDS.

whenToCallPro: DPF replacement requires programming and EPA compliance.

faq.a: If cracked it cannot be cleaned, only replaced.

title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Performance
shortDescription: Turbo boost control system response is out of range.
fullDescription:
6.7L sets P132B for VGT actuator response failures. The smart actuator reports its own faults via dedicated bus.

Ford TSB updates have addressed many false sets; ensure latest calibration.
whenToCallPro: PCM reflash and actuator initialization need IDS.

faq.a: Yes, Garrett supplies the OE unit, common rebrands available.

title: EGR A Control Stuck Open
shortDescription: EGR valve cannot return to closed position.
fullDescription:
Carbon binding the EGR valve butterfly is the leading cause on 6.0L and 6.4L. Stuck-open EGR causes rough idle, smoke, and combustion issues.

6.7L has a different valve design but suffers similar carbon buildup.

fixSteps.title: Remove and inspect EGR valve
fixSteps.instruction: Look at butterfly motion, soak in carb cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Replace EGR valve if cleaning fails
fixSteps.instruction: New valve with new gaskets, torque to spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect EGR cooler
fixSteps.instruction: Heavily plugged cooler may need replacement.

whenToCallPro: EGR cooler replacement on 6.0L is dealer-level.
videoSearchQuery: Power Stroke P042E EGR stuck open

faq.a: No, EGR delete is illegal in US/Canada.

title: Fuel Delivery Error
shortDescription: Fuel delivery system has not met commanded targets.
fullDescription:
Generic delivery error on 6.0L commonly tied to HPOP (high-pressure oil pump) or IPR (injection pressure regulator) failures. 6.4L/6.7L use this code for common rail issues.

Check ICP/IPR live data first on 6.0L.

fixSteps.title: Check ICP at crank (6.0L)
fixSteps.instruction: Forscan live data; need 500+ psi to fire.

fixSteps.title: Replace stand pipes and dummy plugs
fixSteps.instruction: Common 6.0L failure point under turbo, soaks oil.

fixSteps.title: Replace IPR
fixSteps.instruction: Side of HPOP, replace with new O-rings.

partsNeeded.part: Stand pipe and dummy plug kit

videoSearchQuery: Power Stroke 6.0 P0148 stand pipe IPR

faq.a: Yes, common preventive job at 100k miles.

title: PCM Processor Fault
fullDescription:
Internal processor error in the engine control module. Often caused by water intrusion (FICM box on 6.0L) or aged solder joints.

6.0L FICM is famous for failure - check power supply first (need 48V at crank).

fixSteps.title: Test FICM voltage (6.0L)
fixSteps.instruction: Should show 48V during cranking via Forscan.

fixSteps.title: Replace FICM power supply
fixSteps.instruction: Aftermarket 6/7 Diesel power supply board, solders into existing FICM.

fixSteps.title: PCM replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Dealer programming required after PCM swap.

whenToCallPro: PCM replacement requires Ford dealer programming.

faq.a: Yes, FICM voltage drop is the most common 6.0L cold-start complaint.
